newsitem.title: USA: Rival prods Thurmond to show he is mentally fit.
newsitem.headline: Rival prods Thurmond to show he is mentally fit.

text.p: Democratic candidate Elliott Close Thursday dropped a bid to debate Sen. Strom Thurmond and instead challenged the 93-year-old Republican to tell South Carolina voters his vision for the next century.
Close, 43, a political newcomer, has used Thurmond's age as a weapon during the campaign, charging that his opponent is too old to keep the job he has had for more than four decades.
Thurmond, first elected to the Senate in 1954, is the oldest person in Congress. If he is re-elected and serves an eighth six-year term, he will be the longest-serving senator ever.

Close, a real estate developer and heir to the Springs Industries textiles fortune who has never held elected office, told Reuters he had dropped any hopes of a public debate with Thurmond but he prodded the Republican to face journalists by himself in a live, 90-minute question-and-answer session.
Close said that would enable Thurmond to "put to rest once and for all any question about his ability to lead South Carolina into the next century."
Thurmond turned down the idea, saying in a statement the only campaign issue was whether voters Nov. 5 would elect "a conservative experienced senator or an inexperienced liberal."

In television advertising and during his campaign speeches, the Democrat has questioned whether Thurmond can still handle the rigours of Washington politics. "People deserve to hear their senior senator talk unscripted about the issues," Close said.

Thurmond says he has not debated any opponent for decades because he does not want to give them publicity, but he often meets voters during appearances across the state and spent two days this week travelling by bus to meet voters in 10 counties.

On Monday, in Laurens, South Carolina, Thurmond came face-to-face with Close, who had pushed his way to the front of the crowd to shake his opponent's hand. Close asked the senator about a debate, but Thurmond ignored him.
The incident prompted Close to end his call for debates on the grounds that Thurmond seemed "startled and shaken" by his presence on the campaign trail.
Thurmond's political consultants said Close's statements reflected his desperation.
